text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Friday it had not received underwriting support for its capital raising but it continued to reject the 75 cents a share takeover offer from Placer Dome Inc.

Placer Dome said in a separate statement its offer was final and it has withdrawn its offer to buy Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea (PNG) for A$316.1 million, which equates to 56 cents per Highlands share.

"We are disappointed that this underwriting failed, but we remain committed to our A$0.75 a share offer for Highlands," Placer Dome president and chief executive officer John Willson said in a statement.
"Placer Dome's offer price for Highlands of 75 cents is final. There will be no increase," Willson said.
The offer is scheduled to remain open until January 18.

Highlands' proposed underwriting was to raise A$160 million at 30 cents a share and was necessary to enable the Highlands group restructure, which included a new company Highlands Pacific Ltd being created to own the non-Porgera assets.

"The restructuring proposal put by Highlands Gold to Placer has been unable to proceed despite strong support from financial institutions, particularly in Papua New Guinea, as there was insufficient commitment from institutions in Australia in the limited time available," Highlands said.
It said the recent gold price fall contributed to investor caution in relation to the proposal.
Highlands said an extension of the underwriting deadline was sought from Placer, but was rejected.
Under the planned restructure Highlands Pacific was to develop the Ramu nickel/cobalt and Frieda-Nena copper and gold projects in PNG.

"The significant support for the Highlands Pacific issue received from institutional investors endorses the board's view that the value of Highlands' Ramu and Frieda-Nena projects and the extensive exploration portfolio in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia is far in excess of the value implied for these assets by Placer's current takeover offer of A$0.75 per share."
"Accordingly, the board of Highlands continues to recommend that shareholders reject Placer's totally inadequate offer," Highlands said.
Placer Dome owns more than 40 percent of Highlands following the launch of its takeover bid for the PNG miner on November 27, 1996.
Highlands shares were last traded three cents lower at 78 cents prior to a trading halt in mid-afternoon trade before the result of the underwriting proposal.
